thread:
Jules (customer): Hey team — we're seeing reproducible SSE streams abort mid-generation when the user switches networks (Wi‑Fi -> LTE). Partial chunks arrive (we get 2–3 tokens) then connection closes. Happened on iOS app (React Native WebView) and one Android device. Request id: req_01GZ9q8a. Sample client log: 

[client] stream.onclose: code=1006, reason=EOF, msg="stream closed by peer"
received chunk: "Hello, wor"

Happens reliably if user toggles wifi or moves out of range during generation. Any known workarounds?

Samir Patel: Thanks for the report — can you attach the full request id + approximate repro steps? Are you using our JS SDK or a raw EventSource? Also which model, token limits, and whether you're passing any streaming callbacks (progress hooks)?

Jules (customer): Using our homegrown EventSource wrapper in a RN WebView (iOS 17.2). Steps to repro: 1) open chat, 2) start generation, 3) pull down control center and toggle wifi off -> device switches to cellular; 4) stream closes immediately. Model: open-llm-7b (hosted); max_tokens: 512. Request id again: req_01GZ9q8a. Here's the client snippet we use: 

```
const es = new EventSource(url, { withCredentials: true });
es.onmessage = e => handleChunk(e.data);
es.onerror = e => { console.log('SSE error', e); es.close(); };
```

Samir Patel: Got it. Two quick asks: 1) can you paste the server-side logs around req_01GZ9q8a (we'll look for connection handoffs/fallbacks), and 2) include any TLS/HTTP2 settings (are you using http2 via the webview?).

OpsBot: Log snippet uploaded to thread: 

```
2026-02-12T14:03:12.842Z request=req_01GZ9q8a model=open-llm-7b stream=started client_ip=54.122.11.9
2026-02-12T14:03:20.117Z request=req_01GZ9q8a stream=chunk_sent seq=1 size=24
2026-02-12T14:03:21.452Z request=req_01GZ9q8a stream=chunk_sent seq=2 size=18
2026-02-12T14:03:21.873Z request=req_01GZ9q8a connection=closed_by_client reason=network_change
2026-02-12T14:03:21.874Z request=req_01GZ9q8a stream=terminated tokens_sent=42
```

Jin Park: Looks like client-side TCP reset on network interface change. Mobile OSes will often tear down sockets on IP stack change; HTTP/2 can aggressively reset streams. That matches the close_by_client reason. Important notes: 
- SSE itself (EventSource) can't resume mid-generation — there's no server-side tokenized resume (we don't store partial KV state keyed by client).
- Workarounds: implement client reconnect + idempotent restart or chunking at the application layer. For conversation UIs we recommend sending the full prompt again but with a small prefix dedupe: e.g., upon reconnect send prompt_prefix = last_confirmed_text and server-side logic to de-duplicate identical prefix tokens.

Maya Rodriguez: On the infra side we can also temporarily increase keepalive/ping frequency on the ingress for these customers to detect stale connections earlier, but that won't prevent TCP resets from an interface change. Also adding a short grace period on the backend to accept near-immediate reconnections with an idempotency_key could reduce double-tokens when clients retry quickly.

Samir Patel: For immediate mitigations for your iOS RN WebView: 
- Switch to a WebSocket fallback for streams where you need resiliency across mobile network changes (WS will still drop on network change but client libs often have reconnection + resume logic).
- Implement client-side exponential reconnect and show partial progress to user. Example (JS pseudo):
```
let retry = 0;
function connect() {
  const es = new EventSource(url);
  es.onmessage = e => { retry = 0; handleChunk(e.data); };
  es.onerror = () => { es.close(); if (retry < 5) setTimeout(connect, Math.pow(2, retry++) * 200); }
}
connect();
```
- If you must avoid duplicate output, on reconnect re-request generation with an explicit dedupe prefix and drop tokens that match.

Jules (customer): Thanks — do retries incur extra billing? Our UX team is worried about cost for frequent restarts if network is flaky.

Samir Patel: Retries are billed like any other inference request (tokens produced count). Workarounds to limit cost: reduce chunk size (lower token streaming buffer), lower temperature to shorten outputs, and use shorter max_tokens so partial restarts are cheaper. We'll also explore an internal opt-in idempotency feature for streams (engineering ticket).

Jin Park: I'm filing a bug for the RN WebView + iOS socket behavior (assigning to mobile-eng). Action items: 1) mobile-eng to add client reconnect examples to our SDK docs, 2) support to offer short-term config tweaks for customers (increase keepalive), 3) infra to prototype idempotency window.

Jules (customer): Appreciate the quick help — we'll try the reconnect strategy and report back. :thumbsup:

Maya Rodriguez: Noted. I'll follow up here after we have a short-term config we can toggle per-customer.

Samir Patel: If you can paste one reproducible build+device we can attempt an internal repro on Monday. Cheers.
